How to use the slab cost calculator

  1. Enter slab length, width and thickness and a waste allowance (10 % is typical).
  2. Type the prices from your local store or supplier. Leave a price blank if you do not know it.
  3. Compare the cost of bags with a ready-mix truck. Gravel base and wire mesh are added to every option.

Formula

Volume = length × width × thickness, plus waste. Bags = volume ÷ bag yield, rounded up. Yields (Quikrete): 80 lb ≈ 0.60 ft³, 60 lb ≈ 0.45 ft³, 40 lb ≈ 0.30 ft³.

Example: 10 ft × 10 ft × 4 in with 10 % waste = 36.67 ft³ = 1.36 yd³, which is 62 bags of 80 lb.

Tips

  • Above about 1 yd³, a ready-mix truck is usually easier than mixing dozens of bags; ask about short-load fees.
  • Use 4 in for patios and walks and 5–6 in for driveways or heavy loads.
  • Prices vary widely by region, so this calculator never fills them in for you.

FAQ

How many bags of concrete for a 10 × 10 slab?

At 4 in thick with 10 % waste you need about 62 bags of 80 lb, 82 bags of 60 lb or 123 bags of 40 lb.

When is ready-mix cheaper than bags?

Usually above about 1 to 1.5 yd³, but it depends on your local bag price, ready-mix price and delivery fee. Enter them to compare.

Why are the prices empty?

Concrete prices change by region and season. Enter your own prices so the comparison is accurate.

Do I need a gravel base?

Most slabs sit on 4 in of compacted gravel for drainage and support. Enter the depth and price to include it.

Does the cost include tools and labor?

No. It covers concrete, gravel and mesh only. Add forms, rebar, tool rental and labor separately.
